_note: Engine-level constants the design handoff did not specify. Kept out of the design's own JSON files so those stay exactly as delivered. Still content, not code — CLAUDE.md forbids balance constants living in source.

combat._hitClipNote: How long the recoil clip plays, and how hurt an enemy has to be before it switches to its injured walk. Both are RENDER-ONLY -- neither changes damage, speed or any decision the sim makes, so tuning them cannot move balance. `injuredBelowPct` is a percentage of max hp; a sheet with no `walkHurt` clip simply keeps walking normally, which is what makes it safe to ship before every animal has the art.
combat._hitFlashNote: The flash is 60ms as the spec asks, but 60ms only reads as a blink if it is allowed to end. It was re-armed on every hit INCLUDING damage-over-time ticks, so at late-wave fire rates it never expired: wave 15 with 266 enemies rendered most of the crowd as solid white silhouettes and the wave-12 boss could not be seen at all while being fought. DoT no longer flashes, and the refractory caps the duty cycle at 60/(60+160) = 27%, so a hit reads as a blink against the sprite rather than replacing it. Raise the refractory if a crowd still washes out; lower it if single hits stop registering.

camera._zoomNote: Zoom is derived, not fixed: round(canvasHeight / targetWorldHeight), integer only, clamped. A fixed zoom made screen size and DPI control HOW MUCH WORLD you see - at 1920x1080 dpr 1.5 the view was 810 world px tall, so the farmer was 2% of screen width and every round a speck. 560 lands on ~540 world px on every screen from 1080p to 4K, which is the SAME view a 1080p dpr-1 screen always had: the framing that was already right, now independent of monitor and DPI. It is deliberately NOT tighter - the rounds were made legible by packing bigger art, not by cropping the field, and cropping costs you the warning time to see a horde coming. Small screens bottom out at minZoom and show less; that is the integer-zoom floor, not a target.

fx._note: Conformed FX clips (art/sprites.json -> fx). `life` is how long the whole clip plays, in seconds — the renderer divides it by the clip's packed frame count, so retiming an effect is this number and nothing else. Effects are decoration: when the pool is full the sim drops them silently rather than perturbing a seeded run.
fx._rates: Hit sparks on every hit would be 200 sparks a frame in a late wave and would bury the enemies. `hitSparkChance` is the fraction of non-crit hits that spark; crits always do, because a crit is the thing you want to notice.
fx._ring: The weapon ring drawn around the player. radius is how far the icons sit from the player's centre, scale shrinks the 32px source art to something that reads beside a 32px character, and recoil is how far a weapon kicks back along its aim when it fires.
fx._newClips: Clips from the unTied projectile packs. shockwave replaces the conformed FX-pack ring for ground pulses; arrowImpact and bigImpact are the dedicated impact animations those packs ship, which the FX pack had no equivalent of.
fx._ringScaleNote: Ring icons are normalised to weaponRingTargetWidth rather than scaled by a flat factor, because the sources differ: a 32px tool icon and a ~20px gun drawn to be held need different multipliers to end up the same size on screen.
fx._weaponRingSpreadNote: The ARC the weapons fan across, centred on the direction the character faces (down/front). 360 puts them on a perfect circle at even spacing, which reads as an ORBIT — a thing going around him — rather than as gear carried at his sides. Leaving a gap behind the head is most of the difference, and it costs nothing.

playerMark._note: The mark under the player's feet, and the only thing on the field that is his alone. Enemy humanoids share his rig, and repainting the farmhand fixed his CLOTHES without giving the eye anything positive to lock onto in a crowd -- so this is the other half: a soft contact shadow with a faint lamp ring around it, drawn once per frame in the ground layer under every sprite, exactly where the dash dust goes. Nothing else in the game draws one, so it never needs to compete.
playerMark._restraintNote: This is a farm at dusk, not a MOBA. The numbers below are deliberately near the bottom of what still reads: the shadow does most of the work by GROUNDING him, the ring only has to survive a squint. Raise ringAlpha before raising ringWidth -- a thick ring reads as UI drawn over the world, a faint wide one reads as lamplight on grass. If it ever starts to look like a selection circle it has gone too far.
playerMark._footNote: NEGATIVE, and measured, not assumed: the character sheets are 32x64 cells drawn from bottom-centre, but the art stands with its feet at cell row 52 -- twelve pixels ABOVE the cell floor (tools/pixellab-cut.ts, and the LimeZu farmer sheets share the baseline). The player origin is therefore the cell floor, not his boots, and an ellipse drawn there reads as a hole he is hovering over; the owner saw exactly that. -10 puts it on the boot row with the couple of pixels of bias that stops it striping the boots.

harvest._note: Proximity harvesting. `radius` is how far from the player a node is worked, before the harvestPct stat widens it. Node HP, payouts and the tool ladder live in nodes.json; this is only the reach and the feedback timing.
harvest._dwellNote: Standing on a node ramps its harvest rate. Flat-rate proximity harvesting rewards running — sweeping twenty nodes at base rate beats working one — which inverted the intent and eroded The Hand's stand-your-ground identity in the balance harness. The ramp makes committing to a seam the efficient play.

offers._note: How the draw is composed, as opposed to what is in it.
offers._weaponWeightNote: Weapons are weighted up against items so merge pressure survives a big item roster. Once weapon slots are full only OWNED weapons can be offered, so a draw is six weapons against forty items; at 22 items that was six against twenty-two. The roster growing from 22 to 40 therefore cut merge opportunities by about a third without anything being rebalanced, and cleared runs stopped reaching tier 4 at all. 1.6 restores the old weapon share. This is the knob to turn when the item count changes again.

_terrainNote: The ground used to be chosen here, one Wang pair for every run. It moved to src/content/maps.json, where each map picks its own ground set, soil set and blight chain. It MOVED rather than being copied: two content files naming the same ground is the same trap as two art groups writing one frame key — the later one silently wins and nothing tells you which is live. The renderer and tools/draw-world.ts both read the world's map now. The reasoning that picked the Home Field's pair is carried over with it: dirt_to_grass_plain over dirt_to_grass and _flat, because the first carried a repeating motif at 32px that read as wallpaper and _flat replaced it with a regular grid weave, subtler but still a repeat. _plain has none, and the argument is not only that — the ground is what two hundred enemies and their bullets are read AGAINST, so a busy floor costs legibility exactly when the screen is fullest. Interest belongs in the props and decals on top of it.
